title: The safest course is to confess our ignorance: 'Such knowledge is too wonderful for me' (Psalm 139, Sirach 3)
source_text: XLIII. Itaque cum rem tantam scrutanti, undique se tenebrae offundant, & occurrant tricae ac pedicae, ex quibus nos non satis extricare valemus, nihil magis tutum & ingenuum puto, quam ignorantiam nostram hic aperte profiteri, & serio illud Davidis usurpare, Mirabilis facta est scientia tua prae me, & sublimior, quam ut assequi possim. Ac quanquam aliorum ingenia nolim ex mea tenuitate metiri, & super hac re modestam disquisitionem damnare; facile tamen adducor ut credam mysterium hoc ad ea pertinere, de quibus dicit sapiens, Altiora te ne quaesieris, & fortiora te ne scrutatus fueris. Nec mirum videri debet, si mens nostra tam angustis limitibus definita, percipere non possit qua ratione intellectus divinus, cui plane nulli sunt fines, ea cognoscat & attingat quae sunt a cognitione nostra remotissima.
pass_a_gloss: XLIII. Therefore since to one searching so great a matter, darkness spreads itself on every side, and there meet tangles and snares, from which we are not able sufficiently to extricate ourselves, I think nothing more safe and ingenuous, than openly to profess our ignorance here, and in earnest to use that saying of David, Thy knowledge is made wonderful above me, and higher, than that I can attain. And although I would not measure the wits of others by my own slenderness, and condemn a modest inquiry on this matter; yet I am easily led to believe that this mystery pertains to those things, of which the wise man says, Seek not things higher than thee, and search not out things stronger than thee. Nor ought it to seem wonderful, if our mind defined by such narrow limits, cannot perceive by what reason the divine intellect, to which there are plainly no bounds, knows and attains those things which are most remote from our knowledge.
pass_b_english: Anyone who searches into so great a matter finds darkness closing in on every side, and meets tangles and snares from which we cannot properly free ourselves. I therefore think nothing is safer or more honest than to confess our ignorance openly here and to take David's words in earnest: 'Your knowledge is too wonderful for me, too high for me to reach.'

I would not measure other people's minds by my own feebleness, nor condemn a modest inquiry into this matter. Still, I am readily persuaded that this mystery belongs among the things of which the wise man says, 'Do not seek what is too high for you, and do not search out what is too strong for you.'

It should not seem surprising if our mind, confined within such narrow bounds, cannot grasp how the divine intellect, which has no bounds at all, knows and reaches things that lie furthest from our knowledge.

lemmas.gloss: openly to profess our ignorance here

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
